subject: Anthropology
title: Homo Economicus Myth
description: A fast breakdown of Homo Economicus Myth for builders.

hook.text: Economics imagines a rational actor who always maximizes profit. Anthropology has never met this person anywhere.

buildup.text: Homo economicus is the model of humans as rational, self-interested maximizers that drives mainstream economic theory.

discovery.text: Cross-cultural studies show that people regularly choose fairness, generosity, and social harmony over pure profit.

twist.text: Homo economicus isn't human nature. It's a cultural ideal specific to modern capitalist societies.

climax.text: The myth of rational economic man blinds us to the diverse ways people actually make economic decisions.

punchline.text: Rational economic man exists only in textbooks.

quiz.question: What is Homo economicus?
options: The model of humans as rational self-interested maximizers

details.summary: Homo economicus — the model of humans as purely rational, self-interested profit maximizers — is a myth that fails to describe how real people behave. Anthropological evidence shows that humans routinely act from generosity, obligation, tradition, emotion.
details.whyItMatters: Debunking homo economicus matters because economic policy built on this false model produces systems that reward selfishness and punish cooperation. More accurate models of human economic motivation can produce better economic institutions.
takeaways: Homo economicus models humans as rational self-interested maximizers
Anthropological evidence shows this model fails to describe real behavior
People act from generosity, obligation, tradition, and moral conviction

faq.question: What evidence disproves the homo economicus model?
faq.answer: Cross-cultural experiments show people routinely share resources, punish unfairness at personal cost, and honor obligations even when irrational. Gift economies, volunteer labor, and mutual aid networks all demonstrate economic behavior driven by social bonds rather than profit maximization.

faq.question: Why does mainstream economics still use the rational actor model?
faq.answer: Its mathematical simplicity makes modeling easier. It provides clear predictions even if they are often wrong. The model persists partly through institutional inertia and partly because it serves ideological purposes — justifying competitive markets as natural expressions of human nature.
